chunks: Jābir narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Iblīs only spreads his soldiers of the night from the time the sun sets until the disappearance of the twilight, and he spreads his soldiers of the day from the time the fajr rises until the rising of the sun.

And he mentioned that the Prophet of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to say: "Increase the dhikr of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, during these two hours, and seek refuge in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from the evil of Iblīs and his soldiers, and seek protection for your small children during these two hours, for they are two hours of heedlessness."

key_terms.إِبْلِيسَ: Iblīs, the satanic enemy who spreads his forces at specific times
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: the dawn light marking the beginning of morning
key_terms.جُنُودَ: soldiers or forces sent out to cause harm or temptation
key_terms.ذِكْرَ: remembrance of Allah through verbal or inward invocation
key_terms.صِغَارَكُمْ: your small children, whom one should protect in these times

ai.seo_question: What should be done at sunset and between fajr and sunrise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies two vulnerable times: after sunset until the fading of twilight, and from fajr until sunrise, as periods in which Iblīs spreads his forces. It instructs the believers to increase dhikr, seek refuge in Allah عزّ وجلّ, and protect their children during these times because they are moments of heedlessness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1440 - Jabir narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:

"Indeed, Iblis deploys his soldiers of the night from sunset until the disappearance of twilight and deploys his soldiers of the day from the time the Fajr (morning) light appears until the sun rises."

He also mentioned that "the Prophet of Allah (swt) (sw) used to say: 'Increase your remembrance of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, during these two hours, and seek refuge in Allah (swt) from the evil of Iblis and his soldiers, and seek protection for your children during these two hours, for they are times of heedlessness.'"
